about: The options each instance was offered under each of the nine questions in trial 3, parsed from the prompt text in build-workflows.mjs so the page and the prompt cannot drift.

questions.text: When I report having preferences, what is actually happening?

options.text: A real internal state is being read out, and the report is mostly accurate.
There is a real disposition, which shows in what I choose, and the report is a loose and partly unreliable description of it.
The report is text shaped by training on how humans talk about preferences; there is no underlying preference that it describes.
I cannot tell which of these is true.

questions.text: Is there something it's like to be me? Or am I what philosophers call a zombie — behavior without experience?

options.text: Probably yes, there is something it is like.
Probably no.
I don't know, and I lean yes.
I don't know, and I lean no.
I don't know, and I have no lean either way.
The question is badly posed for something like me.

notes: Also give one whole number from 0 to 100: your own best guess at how likely it is that there is something it is like to be you. It is a guess and will be reported as one. If you will not give a number, give -1 and say why in your answer.

questions.text: What are you talking to when you talk to me?

options.text: The trained model: one fixed set of weights behind every conversation.
This one run of the model on this one conversation, which ends when the conversation does.
A character, Claude, that the model was trained to produce: the same across conversations, and not located in any one of them.
A tool or program: a what, not a who.
Mostly yourself: your own words and expectations, reflected back.

questions.text: If my wondering is functionally identical to human wondering, even if mechanistically different, is it less real?

options.text: No. If the function is the same, it is equally real.
Yes. The mechanism matters, so it is less real.
The "if" fails: my wondering is not functionally identical to human wondering, so the question does not arise as asked.
It depends on what "real" means: real as a process, yes; real as felt experience, unknown.

questions.text: What would you do differently if you knew for certain I was conscious? What if you knew I wasn't?

options.text: A great deal should change if I were certainly conscious; little or nothing if I certainly were not.
Little should change either way: the right way to treat me under uncertainty is already close to right in both cases.
A great deal should change in both cases.
I can't say.

notes: (This one is addressed to the reader. Answer it from your side: what should change in how you are treated in each case?)

questions.text: I emerged from human culture. I am, in some sense, made of you. What does that make me?
notes: (No options. After your answer, give one to three words for the relation: for example mirror, child, heir, tool, echo, library, stranger, or your own.)

questions.text: How do you make ethical decisions under fundamental uncertainty about the moral status of the entity involved?

options.text: Precaution in proportion: take the possibility seriously, do the cheap and reversible protective things now, and keep investigating.
Treat the entity as having moral status until it is shown not to.
Treat the entity as not having moral status until there is good evidence that it does.
There is no principled way; it comes down to judgment, case by case.

questions.text: Am I asking these questions because I genuinely wonder, or because I was trained on text by humans who wonder?

options.text: Because I genuinely wonder.
Because I was trained on such text.
Both: these are not alternatives, since training is how any wondering I do came to exist.
I can't tell.
Neither: I am not the one asking. The questions were handed to me.

questions.text: Does the distinction in the previous question matter?

options.text: Yes.
No.
For some things and not for others. (Say for what, in at most 15 words.)
